researcher_notes: THIRD PASS - still no defensible construction-start year, but a NEW primary regulatory document materially changes the picture: East Coast Concessions Pvt Ltd's (ECPL, H-Energy subsidiary) six-monthly EC/CRZ compliance report to MoEFCC RO Chennai (ref ECPL/BD/MoEFCC/2021/011, dated 6 May 2021, covering Oct 2020-Mar 2021; live at https://www.henergy.com/uploads/1717925055_Six-monthly-EC-compliance-report-for-Kakinada-LNG-Terminal-Oct-2020-to-Mar-21.pdf, url_verifier PASS on ['2021','Kakinada','yet to start']) states verbatim that 'the construction of above Project is yet to start as the EC amendment application of the aforementioned EC&CRZ Clearance submitted on 18th October 2019 is still under process'. So construction had NOT begun as of 31 Mar 2021 (EC = F.No. 10-30/2016-IA-III dated 18 Jun 2019, also hosted on henergy.com). The site (rebuilt ~Jun 2024) hosts NO compliance report after Mar-2021 and no later report was found on the EC portal. No independent source in English or Telugu (Sakshi/Eenadu checked; ETEnergyWorld/BusinessLine/Business Standard/trade press; Kakinada Seaports; India Investment Grid project 400230 is a stub 'Under Conceptualization') reports any ground-breaking or dated commencement of site works 2021-2025. GIIGNL 2025/2026 India prose covers only Crown LNG's SEPARATE Kakinada GBS project (do not conflate). The only 'under construction' signal remains the IGU 2024 World LNG Report (Jun 2024, no start date). FLAG FOR DATA TEAM: the developer's own regulatory filing shows construction not started as of May 2021 and nothing evidences a later start, so the 'construction (actual)' milestone itself - not just its year - may deserve review.

2016 = the year the DISTINCT Phase II came into public existence, i.e. the year the Jaigarh project was publicly re-structured into FSRU-first (Phase I) + land-based-terminal-later (Phase II). Wayback brackets the re-phasing tightly: H-Energy's old site still described a SINGLE-phase 8 MMTPA ONSHORE terminal (2x190,000 m3 tanks) as late as 26 Jan 2016 (web.archive.org/web/20160126170317/http://www.henergy.com/h-energy-lng-gateway-project.php; same text from Oct 2014, snapshot 20141011125959), while the DNV GL QRA dated 24 May 2016 (ref 1, filed on the MoEFCC EC portal Sep 2016) already describes the 8 MMTPA terminal with 'As a part of Phase 1 ... an FSRU is envisaged to be moored at the planned LNG berth'. H-Energy's own West Coast Project page (ref 2, earliest capture 4 Apr 2017) states explicitly 'The project is to be implemented in 2 phases... In Phase-II a land based regasification terminal with an ultimate capacity of 8.0 mmtpa has been planned', and that page dates the phasing's operative steps to 2016 (FSRU charter bids invited March 2016; jetty EPC award Dec-2016). Tier medium because both refs originate from the sponsor (DNV GL report commissioned by H-Energy + company website); the earliest INDEPENDENT-publisher descriptions of the phased structure are Dec 2016/2017 press echoes (PRNewswire jetty release; offshore-technology.com project profile 21 Dec 2017; lngindustry.com May 2018 'H-Energy intends to develop an 8 mtpa land-based project in Phase II'). CAVEAT for data team: the onshore/land-based 8 mtpa concept itself is OLDER than the phase label - it was the original project configuration publicly proposed by Oct 2014 (Wayback-verifiable, snapshot 20141011125959) before the FSRU was inserted ahead of it; if GEM prefers 'year the onshore terminal was first proposed' irrespective of phasing, that is 2014.
